title: French high school students protest conditions, block schools nationwide
seoTitle: Paris: French students protest school conditions

tea.why: Students are protesting poor learning conditions, including teacher shortages, overcrowded classrooms, long school days, and dilapidated buildings.
tea.want: Protesters demand better learning conditions, increased resources, more teachers, and improved school infrastructure.
tea.changed: Oct 6: Tens of thousands of demonstrators are expected in Paris as trade unions join students for a nationwide day of protest.

summary: High school students across France have been protesting since mid-September over poor learning conditions. Grievances include a shortage of teachers, overcrowded classrooms, long school days, and deteriorating school buildings. The movement began in the Paris suburbs and has spread nationwide, leading to school blockades and clashes with police. Authorities have reported thousands of arrests, primarily minors, and hundreds of injuries among students, teachers, and police. The government has urged a return to peaceful gatherings while addressing some student demands. Trade unions are joining a major day of protest on October 6.
demands: Review of school timetables and length of school day
response: Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu urged ministers to postpone travel to focus on managing protests, and ordered them to address leading student demands, including replacing absent teachers, reviewing the school day length, and addressing building repairs, with proposals due by the end of October. updates.text: Protests began at Saint-Exupery high school in Creteil, a Paris suburb, in support of striking teachers.
Police reported around 340 demonstrations and over 160 school shutdowns, with university students blocking 30 campuses.
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu convened an emergency meeting to address "urban violence" as unrest spread across hundreds of high schools and dozens of universities.
A Left-wing mayor of a Parisian suburb was filmed dancing with protesters, leading to a complaint for "incitement to commit a crime" by the Paris Police Prefecture.
A 15-year-old protester lost a hand in northern France after a police dispersal grenade detonated, according to regional newspaper La Voix du Nord.
Tens of thousands of demonstrators, including trade unions, are expected to join nationwide protests, with up to 1,800 high schools disrupted.
